subject: Multi-cloud listing: offer fragmentation and region buckets
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud listing: offer fragmentation and region buckets

Team —

We need to lock the approach for how we surface Redwood offers across AWS, Azure and GCP marketplaces. The exec ask is simple: minimize duplication (fewer SKUs to manage), maximize co-sell coverage per cloud, and avoid blocking launches on platform-specific packaging differences. I attached a first-pass SKU/region matrix.

Top constraints I want us to agree on this week:
- Minimal canonical set: do we ship 2 SKUs per cloud (Starter, Enterprise) or 3 (Starter, Scale, Enterprise)?
- Region buckets: do we mirror cloud-region defaults (US, EU, APAC) or do we prefer country-granular listings for co-sell?
- Packaging differences: AWS wants AMI/container vs. Azure a managed SaaS listing; what fields need to differ and what can be canonical?

Proposed (draft):
- Offer tiers: Starter (hosted API, pay-as-you-go), Scale (reserved throughput/Dedicated), Enterprise (private/VPC + premium SLA).
- Cloud-specific SKUs: map Starter->x1, Scale->x2, Enterprise->x3 per cloud, but reuse a single plan id for co-sell tracking where possible.
- Regions: prioritize US / EU (first wave), APAC second wave; country-level for APAC only for Azure/GCP if partner demands.

Please review the attached sku_region_matrix_v1.xlsx and comment with red-lines. Karthik: cost/contracting impact. Ben: co-sell enablement ask and marketplace listing ops. Jonas: timeline and engineering packaging work.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sku_region_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@aws-partners.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud listing: offer fragmentation and region buckets

Thanks Naomi — useful framing. A couple of quick notes from AWS marketplace side that will impact SKU decisions:

1) SKU volume: AWS prefers <3 SKUs per product family to keep AMI/container images and entitlements manageable. Two SKU tiers (Starter / Enterprise) is a clean pattern, but you lose a natural upsell cadence unless you use metered dimensions.

2) Regions vs. geographies: AWS Marketplace listings are regionalized by marketplace region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1 etc.). For co-sell eligibility we recommend listing at the marketplace-level (US, EU, APAC) rather than every country — that keeps the approval process faster.

3) Packaging fields: for SaaS contracts we ask for a canonical product listing (SaaS) and then use Plan IDs to represent Reserved or Dedicated capacity. If you provide a canonical SaaS offering with Plan IDs that map to Dedicated/Private variants, we can do co-sell tracking without separate public SKUs for every variant.

4) Lead times: typical listing approvals + security reviews = 3–6 weeks once we have the final artefacts (product description, pricing tables, plan ids, images, and a signed Marketplace listing agreement).

Questions: do you have an inventory of plan ids you want assigned for the Reserved/Dedicated plans? Also, will Dedicated customers require separate entitlement keys (yes/no)?

Happy to jump on a 30m to walk the team through the AWS packaging constraints — cc'ing Ben for co-sell coordination.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Partner PM, AWS Marketplace
Alyssa.Chen@aws-partners.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@aws-partners.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud listing: offer fragmentation and region buckets

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 08:34 AM Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@aws-partners.com> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi — useful framing. A couple of quick notes from AWS marketplace side that will impact SKU decisions:
>
> 1) SKU volume: AWS prefers <3 SKUs per product family to keep AMI/container images and entitlements manageable. Two SKU tiers (Starter / Enterprise) is a clean pattern, but you lose a natural upsell cadence unless you use metered dimensions.
>
> 2) Regions vs. geographies: AWS Marketplace listings are regionalized by marketplace region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1 etc.). For co-sell eligibility we recommend listing at the marketplace-level (US, EU, APAC) rather than every country — that keeps the approval process faster.

Thanks Alyssa — this is aligned with our expectation. After talking with engineering and finance the tradeoffs are:

- Go with 2 public SKUs per cloud: Starter (metered tokens, hosted), Enterprise (reserved throughput + Private option). We will implement a metered dimension for Scale-like upsell within the Enterprise plan rather than a separate public SKU.

- Region buckets: launch wave 1 = US + EU marketplace listings. APAC will be packaged for GCP/Azure second wave; we will provide country-level listings (e.g., AU, JP) only where local compliance needs it.

- Packaging mapping (draft):
  * AWS: Public SaaS listing with Plan IDs -> Starter (plan: RED-STA-AWS), Enterprise (plan: RED-ENT-AWS). Dedicated/Private will be an entitlement mapped to RED-ENT-AWS with a separate contract id.
  * Azure: Managed SaaS offer with two plans (RED-STA-AZ, RED-ENT-AZ). We'll include a note on private deployment eligibility.
  * GCP: Marketplace SaaS listing, region-first approach for APAC; plan ids RED-STA-GCP, RED-ENT-GCP.

I attached an internal note (marketplace_packaging_notes.docx) with the mapping that engineering needs for packaging and entitlement keys.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: draft co-sell enablement (one-pager + datasheet) and the partner pitch for each cloud — target draft by EOD Fri.
- Jonas: timeline and engineering checklist for listing artefacts (images, plan ids, pricing table) — deliver by Wed next week.
- Naomi: align with Alyssa/Marco on final plan ids and agree on listing approval timeline.

Karthik
Head of GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: marketplace_packaging_notes.docx (docx)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Multi-cloud listing: offer fragmentation and region buckets

Alyssa / Marco — thanks for the rapid feedback. Confirming Redwood's approach so we can move to artefact prep and DocuSign: 

- Public SKUs: 2 per cloud (Starter, Enterprise). We will use plan ids as Karthik outlined: RED-STA-AWS / RED-ENT-AWS; RED-STA-AZ / RED-ENT-AZ; RED-STA-GCP / RED-ENT-GCP.
- Region wave: launch wave 1 = US + EU across AWS/Azure/GCP. APAC wave 2 (target 8–10 weeks later) with country-specific entries where required.
- Entitlements: Dedicated/Private customers will use RED-ENT-* entitlements; separate entitlement keys will be issued (yes).

Next steps / owners:
- Naomi: share final plan id list and HubSpot opp (RED-7890) with marketplace teams; send listing agreement to Alyssa & Marco by EOD Thu.
- Ben: create co-sell one-pager + partner datasheet; draft by Fri COB.
- Jonas: procurement checklist (pricing tables, images, contact emails) — deliver Wed next week.
- Karthik: confirm engineering packaging notes and entitlement key flow by Tue.

Proposed target dates: listing submission (wave 1) week of 2027-06-07; public availability target 2027-06-28 (subject to approvals).

If this covers it, Alyssa please confirm the 3–6 week review cadence you called out and Marco if Azure has any additional blocking items. I'll loop in legal for the listing agreement signature.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
